audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2 and 4 disagree with the mirror audit (malphite__warwick), which set Level 2 to Warwick, Level 3 to Skill, and kept level 6 and everything after with Malphite. This page has Malphite at levels 2 and 3 and Skill at level 6, and whys[2] beside row 2 says your level-3 burst out-trades him.
audit.why: The mirror is explicit, and the prose on this page already argues Warwick wins the early levels — only the chart says otherwise.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2 and 4 flipped on both layers as one atomic group, whys[4] rewritten so level 6 no longer reads as an even skill fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and late spikes credit 'Thunderclap armor scaling' for blunting your damage.
audit.why: Ground Slam (E) is the armour-scaling ability — it deals magic damage based on his Armor AND reduces attack speed, on a flat 7s at every rank. That attack-speed cut is the real anti-Warwick mechanic, because your passive healing and Blade of the Ruined King both ride on attacks. Thunderclap is his W. His R is 130s at rank 1 against your 110s.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam named with its 7s cooldown and its attack-speed reduction in spikes[2].text and the late prose; the 130s ultimate cooldown put into the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thunderclap is labelled '(E)' in spikes[0].text when it is his W; Unstoppable Force is called 'a point-and-click knockup'; and Infinite Duress is called a 'point-and-click fight starter' in phases[4].why and breakdown.late.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force launches him to a LOCATION at high speed, knocking up what it hits — a charge, not a targeted cast, and 1000 range. Infinite Duress is likewise a directional leap suppressing the first champion collided with for 1.5s, flagged as an interruptible channel — which is exactly why his knockup is dangerous to it. Also Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges when he goes unhit, so poking it off before committing is real sequencing.
audit.corrected: Slots fixed, both ultimates restated as what they are, and the Granite Shield threshold stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'Bait Unstoppable Force' in wants.you[1] as a probable wrong name.
audit.why: False positive — Unstoppable Force is Malphite's R.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Malphite's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a 130s charge that knocks up — hard CC aimed at your Duress channel. Bait the charge, then leap onto the first champion in its path.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Malphite carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion in its path for 1.5s, and his knockup threatens that channel — go second. Malphite carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: Before Malphite stacks armor you win the trade war: his Seismic Shard (Q) poke is weak without mana, and your W-empowered Jaws of the Beast plus Eternal Hunger sustain out-damages his Thunderclap (E) when his passive shield is down.
edits.after: Before Malphite stacks armor you win the trade war: Seismic Shard (Q) poke is mana-hungry, and your Blood Hunt Jaws of the Beast plus Eternal Hunger out-damages Thunderclap (W) once his 10% max-health Granite Shield is popped.

edits.before: This is the swing point — Unstoppable Force (R) is a point-and-click knockup that interrupts your Infinite Duress and sets up a full combo, so it becomes a skill fight around dodging or baiting his ult.
edits.after: This is the swing point — Unstoppable Force charges to a location and knocks up, 130s at rank 1, and that hard CC threatens your Duress channel, so bait the charge before you ever leap.

edits.before: Once Malphite rushes armor items his passive shield and Thunderclap armor scaling blunt your AA-reliant damage, and his R combo can burst you; play around his R cooldown rather than raw dueling.
edits.after: Once Malphite rushes armor his Granite Shield and Ground Slam (E, flat 7s) blunt you — that slam scales off his armor and cuts your attack speed, which is your whole damage. Play his 130s R, not the duel.

edits.before: Once Malphite buys armor you fall off: his shield and Thunderclap scaling nullify your on-hit sustain damage and his R deletes you, so past his first item and into full tank he wins outright.
edits.after: Once Malphite buys armor you fall off: Ground Slam scales off it and cuts your attack speed, gutting your on-hit damage, and Seismic Shard steals the move speed you chase with — he wins outright.

edits.before: At 6 Unstoppable Force interrupts your R, making it an even skill fight.
edits.after: At 6 his knockup charge beats your leap and starts his full combo.

notes: Seismic Shard carries a 'grounding' derived flag, but Riot's own description says only that it damages and steals Move Speed for 3 seconds — no grounding anywhere in the text. Treating that flag as a parsing misfire, I wrote the move-speed steal (which is verifiable and matters more here, since it is the tool that kills your Blood Hunt chase) and asserted nothing about grounding. Left unverified, matching the mirror auditor: whether Primal Howl's fear can interrupt Unstoppable Force mid-charge, and whether his knockup actually cancels the Infinite Duress suppression once it has connected — I only wrote that the knockup threatens the channel, which the kit's own channel flag supports.
